scope: Proposition 2.6 (Weak norm equation, including the zero set) of the manuscript “Zero-Plane Rigidity for Einstein Four-Manifolds” (preprints/Zero-Plane-Rigidity-for-Einstein-Four-Manifolds-October-4-2026/einstein-boundary.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 348 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 35a3ab1d3d2458b5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The function e/v, defined to be zero on {v = 0}, belongs to L1(M), and ∆v = 6v(1 − σv) + e − |p|2 v (3) holds as an equality of distributions with an L1 density. The quotient is zero almost everywhere on the zero set. This identity may be tested against bounded Lipschitz functions. The corresponding assertions hold for b.
